newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish government in pay deal with 15,000 workers.
newsitem.headline: Turkish government in pay deal with 15,000 workers.

text.p: The government on Friday struck a pay deal with a small Islamist labour grouping after three months of bargaining but it is still short of an accord with the biggest union confederation.

Anatolian news agency said more than 15,000 members of the pro-lslamist Hak-Is confederation would receive a one-off 11.5-million-lira bonus plus a 38 percent increase for the first six months of the two-year labout contract beginning from January 1, 1997.
The agency quoted State Minister Nevzat Ercan as saying the average pay would initially go up to 66 million lira from 37 million under the new deal.
Ercan said monthly inflation-indexed rises would be given in the remaining 18 months of the contract.
Workers affiliated to the Turk-Is confederation, which has some 500,000 members, have stepped up industrial action in recent days to force the Islamist-led coalition to accept its pay terms.

More than 22,000 workers at Turkey's leading state oil and petrochemical firms began to obstruct the shipment of goods from factories and stopped overtime on Thursday and 34,000 workers connected with the military sector held marches.
Turk-Is is seeking an increase of 42 percent and 11.5 million lira for the initial six months and subsequent inflation indexed rises every six months.
